tasks.title: Migrate Windows Hook Implementation to Rust
tasks.description: Port the existing C++ Windows hooks functionality from Source.cpp to Rust using the windows crate
tasks.details: Port the C++ implementation in InhibitWindowsEvents/Source.cpp to Rust using the windows-rs crate (0.52+). Implement low-level mouse and keyboard hooks using SetWindowsHookExA/W, WH_MOUSE_LL, and WH_KEYBOARD_LL. Handle WM_XBUTTONUP/DOWN for mouse buttons 3,4 and VK_LWIN for Windows key. Include proper error handling and resource cleanup. Use the tauri::async_runtime for Windows message pump to avoid blocking the main thread.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit tests for hook callback functions, integration tests on Windows to verify mouse button 3,4 and Windows key suppression works correctly

subtasks.title: Research and setup windows-rs dependencies and FFI bindings
subtasks.description: Set up the windows-rs crate dependency and establish proper FFI bindings for Windows hook APIs
subtasks.details: Add windows-rs crate (0.52+) to Cargo.toml. Research and implement FFI bindings for SetWindowsHookExA/W, UnhookWindowsHookEx, CallNextHookEx, GetMessage, and related Windows APIs. Set up proper use statements for windows::Win32::UI::WindowsAndMessaging and windows::Win32::Foundation modules. Configure build settings for Windows targets.

subtasks.title: Implement mouse hook callback function with MSLLHOOKSTRUCT handling
subtasks.description: Create the low-level mouse hook callback to intercept mouse button 3 and 4 events
subtasks.details: Implement mouse_hook_proc callback function that handles MSLLHOOKSTRUCT. Filter for WM_XBUTTONUP and WM_XBUTTONDOWN messages. Check XBUTTON1 and XBUTTON2 flags for mouse buttons 3 and 4. Return 1 to suppress the event or call CallNextHookEx to allow it. Handle proper casting between Rust types and Windows API types.

subtasks.title: Implement keyboard hook callback with KBDLLHOOKSTRUCT and VK_LWIN suppression
subtasks.description: Create the low-level keyboard hook callback to intercept and suppress Windows key events
subtasks.details: Implement keyboard_hook_proc callback function that handles KBDLLHOOKSTRUCT. Filter for WM_KEYDOWN and WM_SYSKEYDOWN messages with VK_LWIN virtual key code. Return 1 to suppress Windows key events or call CallNextHookEx for other keys. Handle proper type conversions and ensure the callback signature matches Windows API expectations.

subtasks.title: Create thread-safe hook management with proper install/uninstall
subtasks.description: Implement thread-safe hook installation and cleanup using Windows APIs
subtasks.details: Create HookManager struct with methods for install_hooks() and uninstall_hooks(). Use SetWindowsHookExW with WH_MOUSE_LL and WH_KEYBOARD_LL flags. Store hook handles (HHOOK) in thread-safe containers like Arc<Mutex<>>. Implement proper error handling for hook installation failures. Ensure hooks are uninstalled on application exit to prevent resource leaks.

subtasks.title: Integrate Windows message pump with Tauri's async runtime
subtasks.description: Set up the Windows message pump to process hook events without blocking the main thread
subtasks.details: Use tauri::async_runtime to spawn a dedicated thread for the Windows message pump. Implement GetMessage loop to process Windows messages for hooks. Ensure the message pump thread communicates hook status back to the main application thread. Handle proper thread synchronization and shutdown signals. Prevent the async runtime from blocking Tauri's main event loop.

subtasks.title: Add comprehensive error handling and resource cleanup
subtasks.description: Implement robust error handling and ensure proper resource cleanup for all hook operations
subtasks.details: Add Result<> return types for all hook operations with custom error types. Implement Drop trait for automatic resource cleanup. Add logging using log crate for debugging hook operations. Handle edge cases like hook installation failures, invalid parameters, and Windows API errors. Implement graceful shutdown that ensures all hooks are uninstalled and threads are properly terminated.

tasks.title: Setup SignalDB for Configuration Management
tasks.description: Integrate SignalDB as the state management solution for application configuration
tasks.details: Install SignalDB (@signaldb/core, @signaldb/fs) and set up reactive configuration store. Create config schema with fields: enableWindowsKey (boolean), enableMouseButton3 (boolean), enableMouseButton4 (boolean), enableMouseButton5 (boolean), startMinimized (boolean), startWithWindows (boolean). Implement persistent storage to %APPDATA%/inhibit-windows-events/config.json. Use SolidJS reactivity to sync with SignalDB collections.

subtasks.title: Install SignalDB Dependencies and Setup Basic Store

Implement schema validation using SignalDB's built-in validation or custom validators. Create TypeScript interfaces for type safety. Add default values and validation error handling.

tasks.title: Implement Windows Startup Registration
tasks.description: Add functionality to register/unregister the application for Windows startup
tasks.details: Create Rust functions to manage Windows registry HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run entry. Implement add_to_startup() and remove_from_startup() functions using the winreg crate (0.52+). Expose as Tauri commands to frontend. Handle UAC permissions gracefully and provide user feedback for registry operations.
